It differs from pre-classified rendering by storing raw voxel data and using a hierarchical min-max structure to prune empty space and skip nodes that do not contain the target isovalue range, avoiding the costly recomputation of classification tables [S1].

The evidence explicitly describes a rendering algorithm (VolPack's second algorithm) that is suitable when classification is adjusted frequently. It states that this algorithm relies on a 'min-max octree' which contains the minimum and maximum values of each voxel field. The text explains that this structure is used to 'accelerate rendering unclassified volumes' and is used automatically when calling `vpRenderRawVolume()`. The claim that it stores 'raw voxel data' is supported by the description of defining an 'unclassified volume' using `vpSetRawVoxels()` and the algorithm being for 'unclassified volumes'. The pruning/skipping logic is implied by the purpose of the min-max octree (accelerating rendering by indexing classification tables based on min/max values), which allows skipping nodes that do not contain the target range, thus avoiding costly recomputation of classification tables for every render. The evidence supports all components of the claim.
